chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Declining Jazz at the Philharmonic; Illinois Jacquet in the Basie band
summary: Jones stayed with Basie rather than join Granz's tour since Jacquet had already left, and recalls how Jacquet joined Basie.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh Clayton, he was in the Army too?
He didn't go back after the War.

No, he didn't go back. Then when Norman came through with the Jazz Philharmonic they wanted me to go with them and I would not go, because Illinois Jacquet left Basie's band if I left Basie's band there would have been a tremendous hole, I figured.
What about Jacquet? That's right, he joined Basie during the war.
Did he join Basie after he left Cab or before? After he left Cab I guess it was.
After he left Cab, Jacquet had things playing in The Streets of Paris and Berg's with Billy Berg in California. Billy Berg had three places.
Then he joined Basie. That's when he made the record, 'The King.'
